summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics). This last turn adds two source-grounded invariants of decision formation, recorded without any execution, interpretation or experiment so the run can expire with no uninterpreted receipt: first, commit advancement is gated by the leader's own term - raft.maybeCommit asks the log to commit at entryID{term: r.Term, index: r.trk.Committed()} (raft.go:778-780) and raftLog.maybeCommit only advances when that index is beyond the current commit and the log's term there equals the requested term (log.go:453-462), which is why becoming leader appends an empty entry (raft.go:962-971) and why the read path defers a request while committedEntryInCurrentTerm is false (raft.go:1352-1358, 2062-2065); second, a heartbeat cannot forward a commit index beyond the follower's known match - sendHeartbeat sends min(pr.Match, r.raftLog.committed) and records it (raft.go:692-707) while the follower's maybeAppend clamps what it adopts to min(committed, lastnewi) (log.go:107-130). I also corrected one citation in the second entry before finishing so that every claimed operand is anchored in a source that actually establishes it. Across the run the record now holds nine answered questions with retained receipts and explicit counterevidence (three ReadIndex results including the coalescing starvation and its stale-index child; the empty-Entries and undecodable-proposal abort pair with the unvalidated follower relay; the silent conf-change replacement; the last-voter apply abort; the removed-leader progress stall with step-down control, external-trigger boundary and varied-schedule reproduction; the Node API's deadline-only signal), the response-shape validation as a source-explained negative result, one source-only lease-read answer, and six sourced Behaviour entries including the size-limit drop, the Node.Step local filter and the heartbeat read-context behaviour - with no open necessary gaps and defect validity, CFT relevance and deduplication left to human offline review.
